from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Light propagates as a traveling wave.",
            "Two overlapping waves create interference.",
            "Constructive interference increases wave intensity.",
            "Destructive interference cancels wave amplitude.",
            "This provides the basis for holography."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Wave-Particle Duality and Superposition", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup colors
        c1, c2, c3, c4, c5 = "#00FFFF", "#FF00FF", "#FFFF00", "#FF4500", "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show particle wave as a sine wave pulse.
        wave1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=c1)
        self.place_at_grid(wave1, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(wave1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(c1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Demonstrate wave superposition using two overlapping sine pulses.
        wave2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(3 * x + PI), x_range=[-2, 2], color=c2)
        self.place_at_grid(wave2, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(wave2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(c2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the resultant wave peak where waves constructively interfere.
        # Constructive: sum waves with same phase.
        res1 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 1.0 * np.sin(3 * x), x_range=[-2, 2], color=c3)
        self.place_at_grid(res1, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(VGroup(wave1, wave2), res1))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(c3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show the resultant wave flat where waves destructively interfere.
        res2 = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0, x_range=[-2, 2], color=c4)
        self.place_at_grid(res2, 'E4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Transform(res1, res2))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(c4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Show the concept of a wave function spreading out.
        circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color=c5)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'F4', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Create(circle), circle.animate.scale(2.0).set_opacity(0.3))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(c5)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Physics of Diffraction: Light Bending", 
                          ["Diffraction occurs when light hits obstacles.", 
                           "Huygens principle defines wavefronts as sources.", 
                           "Light spreads into patterns of fringes."])
        self.lecture.set_opacity(1)

        obstacle = Rectangle(height=2, width=0.2, fill_opacity=1, color=GRAY)
        self.place_at_grid(obstacle, "C4")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), Write(waves))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Huygens point sources visualization
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#00FFFF") for _ in range(5)])
        self.place_at_grid(points, "C4")
        self.play(FadeIn(points))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        # Spreading waves
        arcs = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.5 + i*0.2, angle=PI/2, start_angle=-PI/4, color="#00FFFF") for i in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(arcs, "C5")
        self.play(Create(arcs))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Interference Patterns as Information", [
            "Holography is recorded interference patterns.", 
            "We use reference and object beams.", 
            "The pattern captures phase and amplitude.", 
            "It stores information about the object.", 
            "The image is essentially frozen light."
        ])
        
        # Setup waves
        wave1 = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1+i*0.2, stroke_width=2, color="#00FFFF") for i in range(5)])
        wave2 = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.1+i*0.2, stroke_width=2, color="#00FFFF") for i in range(5)])
        self.place_at_grid(wave1, 'C2', scale_factor=1)
        self.place_at_grid(wave2, 'C5', scale_factor=1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(wave1), FadeIn(wave2))
        self.play(wave1.animate.shift(RIGHT*1), wave2.animate.shift(LEFT*1), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        # Placeholder for interference pattern representation
        fringes = VGroup(*[Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color="#FFFF00" if i % 2 == 0 else "#000000", stroke_width=3) for i in range(10)])
        fringes.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(fringes, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(fringes))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(wave1.animate.shift(UP*0.5), run_time=1)
        self.play(fringes.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=1)

        self.lecture[2].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[3].set_opacity(1)

        self.lecture[3].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[4].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(wave1), FadeOut(wave2), fringes.animate.set_opacity(0.5))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Reconstruct by illuminating the hologram.", "Light diffracts to recreate wavefronts.", "Viewers see true 3D perspective.", "The image floats in space.", "Perspective shifts as viewers move."]
        self.setup_layout("Holographic Reconstruction: Decoding the Pattern", lecture_lines)
        
        # Reveal lecture lines sequentially
        for line in self.lecture:
            self.play(FadeIn(line))

        # Assets
        hologram_plate = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        laser_beam = Line(LEFT*2, RIGHT*0.5, color="#00FF00", stroke_width=4)
        reconstructed_obj = Sphere(radius=0.8, color="#00FFFF").set_fill("#00FFFF", opacity=0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(hologram_plate, "C4")
        self.place_at_grid(laser_beam, "C3")
        self.play(Create(hologram_plate), GrowFromPoint(laser_beam, LEFT*4))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(reconstructed_obj, "C6")
        self.play(FadeIn(reconstructed_obj))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3, 4, 5 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Rotate the object to simulate perspective
        self.play(Rotate(reconstructed_obj, angle=PI/4, axis=UP), run_time=2)
        self.play(Rotate(reconstructed_obj, angle=-PI/4, axis=UP), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Future of Data and Imaging", [
            "Holograms secure modern financial banknotes.",
            "Medical imaging utilizes holographic depth.",
            "High-density data storage future."
        ])
        
        # Define assets
        # Asset 1: Interference Pattern for banknotes
        banknote_pattern = VGroup(*[Line(UP, DOWN, color="#00FFFF").shift(RIGHT * i * 0.1) for i in range(-5, 6)])
        self.place_in_area(banknote_pattern, 'A1', 'C3')
        
        # Asset 2: High density data dots
        data_storage = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF00FF", radius=0.05).move_to(self.grid['D1'] + np.array([i*0.1, j*0.1, 0])) for i in range(10) for j in range(5)])
        self.place_in_area(data_storage, 'D1', 'F3')
        
        # Asset 3: Medical Wavefront
        wavefront = VGroup(*[Annulus(inner_radius=0.1, outer_radius=0.15, color="#FFFF00").move_to(self.grid['C4']) for _ in range(3)])
        self.place_in_area(wavefront, 'A4', 'F6')

        # Sequential reveal
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_opacity(1), FadeIn(banknote_pattern))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_opacity(1), FadeIn(wavefront))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_opacity(1), FadeIn(data_storage))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Light: Principles of Diffraction and Holography

sections.title: Prerequisite: Wave-Particle Duality and Superposition
sections.content: Briefly review the wave nature of light. Explain that light propagates as a wave, and when two waves overlap, they interfere (constructive/destructive). This is the 'foundation' for the complex patterns we will see later.
sections.example: Visualize two pebbles dropped into a pond; notice how their ripples cross each other to create new, complex patterns.

sections.title: The Physics of Diffraction: Light Bending Around Obstacles
sections.content: Define diffraction as the phenomenon where light waves encounter an aperture or obstacle. Introduce the Huygens-Fresnel principle: every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical waves.
sections.example: An animation showing a laser beam passing through a tiny slit, widening into a pattern of dark and bright fringes instead of just a straight line.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Interference Patterns as Information
sections.content: Explain that holography is essentially 'frozen interference.' We record both the amplitude and the phase of the light reflected from an object by interfering it with a reference beam.
sections.example: A 3D graphical animation showing a reference beam meeting a 'scattered' beam from a toy robot, creating a complex 'interference fringe' map on a recording plate.

sections.title: Holographic Reconstruction: Decoding the Pattern
sections.content: Explain the final step: how illuminating the recorded fringe pattern with the original reference beam diffracts the light back into the viewer's eyes to recreate the 3D wavefront of the original object.
sections.example: A 'magic window' concept: a user moving their head around a hologram of a dragon to see different perspectives, just as if the dragon were physically floating in the air.

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Future of Data and Imaging
sections.content: Summarize how these principles extend to medical imaging, security (banknotes), and high-density optical data storage.
sections.example: Show a smartphone security hologram shifting colors, followed by a quick visual of a futuristic holographic medical display for surgeons.
